revision.summary: Retain Mazur's degree-one formal-immersion route while recording checked but uncredited foundation slices: canonical-linear coherent H0/H1 with pointed proper-curve H1 finiteness; the associated fppf sheafification of the all-degree normalized Picard presheaf together with an honest absolute Picard degree kernel and splitting; a genuine four-chart affine Weierstrass addition cover with all six exact pairwise compatibilities and an actual glued affine-pair morphism, now identified with the standard member of an actual four-member cover of the full projective product; generic finite free-translation quotient geometry over affine noetherian bases; terminal proper-model specialization at five; and represented polynomial-cusp sections. Proper coherent H0 finiteness, linear connecting maps, Riemann-Roch, proper base change, a pullback-compatible relative degree and relative Pic⁰, Picard representability, addition formulas on the other three projective-product members and the group laws for the global Weierstrass law, actual canonical cyclic and Eisenstein quotient instances, torsion injectivity, represented X_0, and compactification remain open.

nodes.title: Cyclic subgroup quotients and classifying data
nodes.summary: Construct the canonical commutative group scheme on the concrete projective Weierstrass cubic, the finite-flat cyclic subgroup generated by an exact-torsion point, and the quotient with only the kernel and base-change laws exercised by the X_0 and order-49 consumers. The ordinary D(x₁ - x₂) secant chart and D(B₁₂) product-neighbourhood chart carry actual over-base addition morphisms, with B₁₂ := y₁ + y₂ + a₁x₁ + a₃; their restricted projective morphisms agree on the exact intersection, and the second restricts to tangent doubling on the diagonal. Two denominator-cleared infinity-output charts extend those formulas across inverse pairs. All six pairwise restrictions of the four charts agree as actual scheme morphisms on their pullbacks, nonsingularity proves that the four principal opens cover the entire affine-pair presentation, and those charts are glued to an actual morphism from that affine-pair scheme into the concrete projective cubic. The full projective product is now covered by the four products of the genuine Y ≠ 0 and Z ≠ 0 cubic charts, and its standard-by-standard member is canonically identified with the affine-pair presentation and consumes the glued morphism. Actual addition morphisms on the other three product members meeting infinity, their overlap equalities, the global gluing, the commutative group laws, and coordinate-point comparison remain open. Separately, an actual finite free-translation quotient of a supplied commutative group scheme transfers geometric integrality, local finite type, flatness, separatedness, properness, and smoothness under the theorem-specific source hypotheses, together with an affine diagonal, finite section action, stable affine atlas, and scheme-theoretic freeness; the local-finite-type, proper, and smooth results use an affine noetherian base. The field-level abelian-variety quotient is its named consumer. This generic substrate does not instantiate the canonical Weierstrass source, exact-torsion subgroup, desired cyclic quotient, or its arbitrary-base-change kernel law. At the point-group level, no equality between quotient-scheme K-points and the quotient of K-points is asserted without controlling the H1 connecting class.

Construct the abelian-variety Neron substrate at the required arithmetic DVRs, then realize the actual optimal Eisenstein quotient and its cusp-normalized map in that model for the rank-zero and collision consumers. The marked source point's exact-order reduction at 5 is already checked independently and does not require a source elliptic Neron model.

reviewed_against.source: MIT STAGE seminar, Mazur's theorem on torsion, Fall 2023
reviewed_against.finding: The seminar's proof sequence separates integral modular curves, Jacobians, Neron models, finite-flat group schemes, the Eisenstein ideal, and the final formal-immersion argument in the same foundational order retained here.
The lecture sequence corroborates the modular-curve, Jacobian, Neron-model, admissible-group-scheme, and Eisenstein-quotient spine; it does not remove those represented-object dependencies.

The winding quotient replaces delicate Eisenstein descent, but its finite-rational-points theorem proceeds through the winding element in relative homology, Heegner points, Gross-Zagier, Kolyvagin, and analytic nonvanishing.
